newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Tunisian premier signs trade accord with Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian premier signs trade accord with Morocco.

text.p: Visiting Tunisian Prime Minister Hamed Karoui on Thursday signed a trade and tariff agreement with Morocco to boost economic ties between the two countries, the official MAP news agency said.

Karoui, who arrived on Tuesday in Morocco for a three-day visit was received by King Hassan in Rabat and conferred with other Moroccan officials, including the Casablanca-based Confederation of Businessmen, MAP said.
The agency gave no details of the accord content.
Karoui's visit aimed also at preparing the ground for a future official visit of Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali to Morocco, a Western diplomat said.
Relations between Rabat and Tunis reached a low level in the last three years due to differences over several regional issues including Moslem fundamentalism in North Africa, he added.
The two countries are members of the paralysed North African five-nation Arab Maghreb Union set up in 1989. The other members are Algeria, Libya and Mauritania.
